sets.title: From Vague to Vivid: Weather
sets.titleEs: De vago a vivo: el clima

learn.rule: Revising makes a draft stronger. Replace vague words with exact ones, add signal words, and join sentences that repeat.
learn.ruleEs: Revisar hace más fuerte un borrador. Cambia las palabras vagas por palabras exactas, añade palabras de señal y une las oraciones que se repiten.
learn.model: Weak: The storm was bad. Strong: The storm knocked branches onto the street.
learn.notice: The strong sentence shows what the storm did. The weak sentence only says it was bad.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best revision of 'The weather was nice today.'?

options.text: The weather was very nice today.
The sun was bright, and a cool breeze blew across the field.
The weather was nice and good today.

items.why: A strong revision shows what you see and feel. Choices A and C only add words that are just as vague as nice.
items.whyEs: Una buena revisión muestra lo que ves y sientes. Las opciones A y C solo añaden palabras igual de vagas que nice.

items.prompt: Which phrase makes this sentence more precise?
items.text: We saw a thing in the sky after the rain.

options.text: a thing
a bright rainbow
an object

items.why: Exact nouns paint a clear picture. Thing and object could mean anything, but a bright rainbow tells the reader exactly what was seen.
items.whyEs: Los sustantivos exactos pintan una imagen clara. Thing y object pueden significar cualquier cosa, pero a bright rainbow dice exactamente lo que se vio.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that shows time passing.
parts: The air was warm and wet.
items.model: The air was warm and wet. Soon, dark clouds rolled in.
items.why: The clouds arrived after the warm, wet air, so Soon shows the time order. For example and Instead do not fit this change over time.
items.whyEs: Las nubes llegaron después del aire cálido y húmedo, así que Soon muestra el orden del tiempo. For example e Instead no encajan con este cambio en el tiempo.

items.prompt: Check every change that makes this draft stronger.
items.text: It rained. It was cold. We went in.

options.text: Add the word 'very' before 'cold.'
Change 'It rained' to 'Heavy rain fell on the playground.'
Change 'It was cold' to 'The wind felt icy.'
Take out the word 'cold' to make it shorter.
Begin the last sentence with 'Soon,' so the order is clear.

items.why: The right changes add exact details or a signal word. Adding very or cutting cold does not give the reader any new picture.
items.whyEs: Los cambios correctos añaden detalles exactos o una palabra de señal. Añadir very o quitar cold no le da al lector ninguna imagen nueva.

items.prompt: Put this revised draft in order.
lines: A storm rolled over our school on Friday.
First, dark clouds covered the sun.
Next, heavy rain fell on the playground.
Finally, we ran inside to warm up.
items.why: The opening sentence sets the scene. Then First, Next, and Finally put the events in the order they happened.
items.whyEs: La oración inicial presenta la escena. Luego First, Next y Finally ponen los sucesos en el orden en que ocurrieron.

items.prompt: Which revision fixes the repeated words in this draft?
items.text: Plants need water. Plants need sun. Plants need soil.

options.text: Plants need water, plants need sun, and plants need soil.
Plants need many things.
Plants need water, sun, and soil to grow.

items.why: Joining the ideas removes the repeated words and keeps every fact. Choice A still repeats, and choice B loses the facts.
items.whyEs: Unir las ideas quita las palabras repetidas y conserva todos los datos. La opción A sigue repitiendo y la opción B pierde los datos.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Use exact words, add a signal word, and make it longer with details.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Usa palabras exactas, añade una palabra de señal y hazlo más largo con detalles.
write.text: The volcano was big. It made a lot of stuff. People were scared.

label: I used a signal word like first, then, or as a result
Usé una palabra de señal como first, then o as a result
I used exact words like lava, ash, or erupted
Usé palabras exactas como lava, ash o erupted
My draft has at least 25 words
Mi borrador tiene al menos 25 palabras
I ended with a period
Terminé con un punto

write.model: The huge volcano erupted early in the morning. First, red-hot lava flowed down the mountain, and thick ash filled the sky. As a result, many families packed bags and left their homes for safer towns.

familyTalk.en: Pick a boring sentence, such as 'We ate food.' Together, rewrite it with exact words so it paints a picture.
familyTalk.es: Escojan una oración aburrida, como 'We ate food.' Juntos, reescríbanla con palabras exactas para que pinte una imagen.

teacherTip.en: Highlight vague words like thing, stuff, and nice in a draft, then let pairs replace each with an exact word.
teacherTip.es: Resalta palabras vagas como thing, stuff y nice en un borrador y deja que las parejas cambien cada una por una palabra exacta.

sets.title: Sharper Sentences: Market Day
sets.titleEs: Oraciones más claras: el día de mercado

learn.rule: Good revisions add exact details, use signal words to show order or contrast, and combine repeated sentences.
learn.ruleEs: Las buenas revisiones añaden detalles exactos, usan palabras de señal para mostrar orden o contraste y combinan oraciones repetidas.
learn.model: Weak: We visited a place. Strong: We visited the harbor museum on Tuesday.
learn.notice: The strong sentence names the place and the day. The weak sentence could be about anywhere.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best revision of 'The town was old.'?

options.text: The town was very old.
The town was old and old.
Brick buildings and a stone clock tower showed the town was very old.

items.why: Choice C gives proof that the town is old. Choice A only adds very, and choice B repeats the same word.
items.whyEs: La opción C da pruebas de que el pueblo es viejo. La opción A solo añade very y la opción B repite la misma palabra.

items.prompt: Which words should replace 'stuff' to make this sentence more exact?
items.text: The farmers sold stuff at the market.

options.text: things
corn, apples, and eggs
items

items.why: Naming the foods tells the reader exactly what was sold. Things and items are as vague as stuff.
items.whyEs: Nombrar los alimentos le dice al lector exactamente lo que se vendió. Things e items son tan vagas como stuff.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that shows a contrast.
parts: The market is open all week.
items.model: The market is open all week. However, the stalls close on Sunday.
items.why: The second sentence is a surprise after the first one, so However fits. Next shows order, and Because shows a reason.
items.whyEs: La segunda oración es una sorpresa después de la primera, así que However es la correcta. Next muestra orden y Because muestra una razón.

items.prompt: Which changes would make this draft stronger? Check all that apply.
items.text: People came to the market. They bought food. They went home.

options.text: Change 'food' to 'fresh bread and apples.'
Add the word 'very' before 'market.'
Change 'People' to 'Some folks.'
Begin the last sentence with 'Finally,' so the order is clear.
Change 'People' to 'Families from nearby villages.'

items.why: Exact details and a signal word make the draft stronger. Some folks is as vague as people, and very market adds nothing.
items.whyEs: Los detalles exactos y una palabra de señal hacen más fuerte el borrador. Some folks es tan vaga como people y very market no añade nada.

items.prompt: Put the revised sentences in order.
lines: Families from nearby villages came to the market on Saturday.
First, they bought fresh bread and apples.
Next, they traded stories with their neighbors.
Finally, they carried their baskets home.
items.why: The opening sentence tells who and when. First, Next, and Finally then show the order of the day.
items.whyEs: La oración inicial dice quién y cuándo. Luego First, Next y Finally muestran el orden del día.

items.prompt: Which sentence best combines these repeated sentences?
items.text: The baker baked bread. The baker baked rolls. The baker baked pies.

options.text: The baker baked bread, the baker baked rolls, and the baker baked pies.
The baker baked bread, rolls, and pies.
The baker baked a lot.

items.why: Choice B names the baker once and lists all three foods. Choice A still repeats, and choice C drops the foods.
items.whyEs: La opción B nombra al panadero una sola vez y enumera los tres alimentos. La opción A sigue repitiendo y la opción C quita los alimentos.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Use exact words, add a signal word, and make it longer with details.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Usa palabras exactas, añade una palabra de señal y hazlo más largo con detalles.
write.text: The town had a festival. Some people came. They did things.

label: I used a signal word like first, next, or also
Usé una palabra de señal como first, next o also
I used exact words like music, food, or parade
Usé palabras exactas como music, food o parade
My draft has at least 25 words
Mi borrador tiene al menos 25 palabras
I ended with a period
Terminé con un punto

write.model: The town held a harvest festival in October. First, families from nearby villages arrived with baskets of apples and pumpkins. Next, a band played music, and children danced in the square.

familyTalk.en: Tell a family story in one vague sentence, then add a place, a time, and one exact detail to make it clearer.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten una historia familiar en una oración vaga y luego añadan un lugar, un momento y un detalle exacto para que quede más clara.

teacherTip.en: Keep a class chart of vague words and stronger replacements, and add to it after every revision lesson.
teacherTip.es: Mantén un cartel de la clase con palabras vagas y reemplazos más fuertes, y agrégale después de cada lección de revisión.

learn.rule: Revise a story by choosing strong verbs and exact details, adding signal words, and combining sentences that repeat.
learn.ruleEs: Revisa un cuento eligiendo verbos fuertes y detalles exactos, añadiendo palabras de señal y combinando oraciones que se repiten.
learn.model: Weak: Mina walked in. Strong: Mina tiptoed into the dark kitchen.
learn.notice: The strong verb tiptoed shows how Mina moved. The word dark helps you see the kitchen.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best revision of 'Sam went to the door.'?

options.text: Sam went to the door slowly.
Sam tiptoed to the creaky door and gripped the cold handle.
Sam went to the very big door.

items.why: A strong verb and exact details show the scene. Choices A and C add a vague word but no picture.
items.whyEs: Un verbo fuerte y detalles exactos muestran la escena. Las opciones A y C añaden una palabra vaga, pero ninguna imagen.

items.prompt: Which word best shows that Leo felt nervous?
items.text: Leo forgot his line. "I forgot my line," Leo ___.

options.text: said
mumbled
cheered

items.why: Mumbled sounds quiet and unsure, like a nervous speaker. Said is plain, and cheered shows excitement, not worry.
items.whyEs: Mumbled suena bajo e inseguro, como alguien nervioso. Said es neutral y cheered muestra emoción, no preocupación.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that shows a result.
parts: Leo practiced his lines every night.
, he remembered every word on stage.
items.model: Leo practiced his lines every night. As a result, he remembered every word on stage.
items.why: Remembering every word came from the practice, so As a result fits. In contrast would show an opposite, and For example would start an example.
items.whyEs: Recordar cada palabra vino de la práctica, así que As a result es la correcta. In contrast mostraría lo opuesto y For example empezaría un ejemplo.

items.prompt: Select the revisions that would improve this weak draft.
items.text: The girl ran. She was scared. The dog came.

options.text: Change 'ran' to 'sprinted across the dark yard.'
Add the word 'very' before 'scared.'
Change 'She was scared' to 'Her heart pounded.'
Take out 'The dog came.' to make it shorter.
Begin the last sentence with 'Suddenly,' to show the order.

items.why: Strong verbs, a feeling shown with an action, and a signal word improve a draft. Adding very or cutting a sentence leaves the story just as thin.
items.whyEs: Los verbos fuertes, un sentimiento mostrado con una acción y una palabra de señal mejoran un borrador. Añadir very o quitar una oración deja el cuento igual de pobre.

items.prompt: Arrange the revised story lines in order.
lines: Nora stood at the edge of the dark stage.
First, she took a deep breath.
Next, she walked into the bright spotlight.
Finally, she sang her song for the whole crowd.
items.why: The scene is set first. First, Next, and Finally then show Nora's actions in order.
items.whyEs: Primero se presenta la escena. Luego First, Next y Finally muestran las acciones de Nora en orden.

items.prompt: Which revision fixes the repeated words in this draft?
items.text: The cat was soft. The cat was gray. The cat was sleepy.

options.text: The cat was soft and the cat was gray and sleepy.
The cat was.
The cat was soft, gray, and sleepy.

items.why: Choice C names the cat once and keeps all three details. Choice A still repeats the cat, and choice B cuts the details.
items.whyEs: La opción C nombra al gato una vez y conserva los tres detalles. La opción A sigue repitiendo al gato y la opción B quita los detalles.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Use exact words, add a signal word, and make it longer with details.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Usa palabras exactas, añade una palabra de señal y hazlo más largo con detalles.
write.text: The boy opened the box. He saw something. He was surprised.

label: I used a signal word like first, next, or because
Usé una palabra de señal como first, next o because
I used exact words like key, map, or gasped
Usé palabras exactas como key, map o gasped
My draft has at least 25 words
Mi borrador tiene al menos 25 palabras
I ended with a period
Terminé con un punto

write.model: The boy slowly opened the dusty wooden box. First, he saw a shiny gold key lying on a folded map. He gasped with surprise, because he had never seen anything like it.

familyTalk.en: Replace 'said' in a sentence with three stronger verbs, like whispered, shouted, or giggled. Talk about how each changes the feeling.
familyTalk.es: Cambien 'said' en una oración por tres verbos más fuertes, como whispered, shouted o giggled. Conversen sobre cómo cada uno cambia el sentimiento.

teacherTip.en: Read one weak and one strong version aloud and ask students to raise a hand when they can 'see' the scene.
teacherTip.es: Lee en voz alta una versión débil y una fuerte y pide que los estudiantes levanten la mano cuando puedan 'ver' la escena.
